category: sandbox (default) and full KVM VM (vm type)
tier: 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 4 GB disk, default container instance

free_tier.stated: Add a card from the billing page (nothing is charged) and the workspace gets a one-time USD 5 credit, enough to run the first instance around the clock for about a month.
free_tier.notes: credit, and it needs a card on file to be granted

retention.stated: Stopped or sleeping instances bill the disk alone at USD 0.09/GB/month; parked in cold storage at USD 0.03/GB/month on compressed bytes; an instance left suspended for 30 days is permanently deleted.

egress.terms: No egress price and no transfer allowance are published on the page read; metered is recorded as false because nothing is known to be charged per gigabyte, which is an absence of evidence, not a promise of free traffic.

interface_detail: REST API for the lifecycle, SSH into the instance, exec over the API, and an HTTPS URL per published port
tooling: the REST API or SSH; Docker and k3s inside a vm instance; no vendor CLI was read
chaining: The cheapest 2 vCPU / 4 GiB offer found anywhere at USD 4.76 a month, but it is the default container instance, not a VM. The VM type - a real KVM machine with its own kernel - costs 2.5x the compute and lands at USD 11.36 for the same 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 4 GB disk.

limits.value: 4 vCPU ceiling on every instance type; 2 vCPU / 4 GB is the smallest shape
disk is 2-12 GB on the 2 vCPU shape and bills USD 0.09/GB/month

binding_note: The shape ladder stops at 4 vCPU on every type, so the ceiling is the shape; the money wall is that a real VM is 2.5x the container rate.

identity_cost.detail: Card required for the USD 5 credit and for every top-up ('Add a card from the billing page (nothing is charged)'); top-ups run USD 5 to USD 10,000 through Stripe, minimum USD 5. No card hold is stated. Debit acceptance is not stated. A create only checks that one day of balance exists and debits nothing.

reliability_note: Automatic top-up is on by default after the first top-up; when a settle leaves the wallet negative the instances are force-slept and requests return 402 until a top-up.
confidence_note: The rate card, the four shapes, the 2.5x VM multiplier, the per-minute metering, the stopped-disk rate and the card requirement are quoted from the vendor's own documentation read. What would raise it: a probe that creates a vm instance and confirms the 2.5x charge on the ledger.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'vCPU | $0.80 per vCPU per month', 'RAM | $0.70 per GB per month', 'Disk | $0.09 per GB per month', and 'Shape | Price at the default disk | 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM / 2-12 GB disk (the default) | $4.76'
quoted: 'A VM instance is a whole virtual machine with its own kernel ... Its compute is 2.5x the default rate, and disk is unchanged.' and 'time spent stopped or sleeping bills its disk alone'

quoted: 'A `vm` instance is a full Linux virtual machine with its own kernel and KVM hardware virtualization.' and 'Publish a container's HTTP port onto the VM with `docker run -p`, then reach it at https://{id}-{port}.agent37.app'
quoted: '$5 free to start. Add a card from the billing page (nothing is charged) and your workspace gets a one-time $5 credit'
quoted: '4 vCPU is the ceiling on every instance type.'

notes: Two rows live in this provider and the shape decides the verdict. Default (container) 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 4 GB disk: 2 x 0.80 + 4 x 0.70 + 4 x 0.09 = USD 4.76 a month at 730 running hours - the cheapest 2 vCPU / 4 GiB found, but it is a shared-kernel instance. VM 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 4 GB disk: 2.5 x (1.60 + 2.80) + 0.36 = USD 11.36. A VM under USD 5 is impossible because the smallest VM shape is 2 vCPU / 4 GB. Ingress is the other catch: ports are published as HTTPS at {id}-{port}.agent37.app, so no raw TCP listener and no UDP - it cannot be a WireGuard node.

shape.note: container instance; the vm type carries the same shape at 2.5x compute

extras.price_arithmetic: Default container: 730 h x (2 x 0.80 + 4 x 0.70 + 4 x 0.09)/730 = USD 4.76 (the vendor's own monthly figure at the default disk). VM type: 730 h x (2.5 x (2 x 0.80 + 4 x 0.70) + 4 x 0.09)/730 = 2.5 x 4.40 + 0.36 = USD 11.36. 10 h/day = 300/730 of either figure: USD 1.96 container, USD 4.67 VM. Stopped, disk only: 4 GB x 0.09 = USD 0.36 a month.

network_out.ports: HTTP(S) through the vendor proxy at https://{id}-{port}.agent37.app; no raw TCP or UDP ingress was described

session_cap.note: no wall-clock cap; auto-sleep is optional and cuts billing to the disk rate
